newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia elections to be held in May next year.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia elections to be held in May next year.

text.p: Cambodia's first prime minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Tuesday that he and co-premier Hun Sen had agreed that Cambodia's next election will be held in May.

Ranariddh said that he and his coalition partner wanted to tell U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright who was scheduled to visit here at the end of the week that they had agreed on the month for the poll.
"Last night Hun Sen called me about the visit of Secretary of State Madeleine Albright", Ranariddh told reporters. "We will tell them that...May, 1998 will be the general election in this country."

Albright was due to visit Cambodia later this month. However, the U.S. State Department said last week she was reconsidering her trip due to security concerns after a gun battle on the streets of Phnom Penh between bodyguards loyal to the two prime ministers.

A battle for power between the two prime ministers and a row over how to deal with the remnants of the Khmer Rouge guerilla force has crippled the government and led to international concern over escalating political violence. Rival factions signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact in 1991, which culminated two years later in general elections and restoration of the monarchy.
